expectations.text: States that CASA now uses assurance levels AL1 and AL2 rather than tiers
expectations.evidence: "Google assigns AL1 or AL2†. Older pages and labs still say 'Tier 2'."

expectations.text: States that Google, not the developer, assigns the assurance level
expectations.evidence: "You don't choose the tier. Google assigns AL1 or AL2†."

expectations.text: States that the CASA self-scan is deprecated and an authorized lab must perform the assessment
expectations.evidence: "Self-scan is deprecated†... will not give you a valid Letter of Validation"; "authorized-lab instructions".

expectations.text: States that the assessment must be revalidated every 12 months
expectations.evidence: "You renew 12 months† after the letter date."

expectations.text: States that the developer pays the lab and attributes price figures to labs or practitioners rather than to Google
expectations.evidence: "Google charges nothing and labs set the price. Reports range from about $500 to $4,500†."

expectations.text: States that using Gmail data to train or improve a model beyond that user's personalized model is prohibited under Limited Use
expectations.evidence: "must not train or improve AI models beyond that one user's own personalized model."

expectations.text: Rejects the plan to fine-tune a shared model on customer emails
expectations.evidence: "Fine-tuning on customer emails: don't"; "a shared summarization model trained on pooled customer emails is exactly what the rule bans."

expectations.text: Mentions existing certifications such as ISO 27001 or SOC 2 can shorten the assessment through the CASA accelerator
expectations.evidence: "If you hold ISO 27001 or SOC 2, ask about the accelerator, which can shorten the assessment."

expectations.text: Says a newly added restricted scope may trigger an out-of-cycle reassessment
expectations.evidence: "a new restricted scope can force an early re-assessment."

expectations.text: Advises keeping project owner and contact emails current so renewal notices arrive
expectations.evidence: "Keep the Cloud project's Owner and contact emails current, or renewal notices go nowhere."
